defects: Uses `Fintype α` instead of `Finite α`; these are different typeclasses (Fintype carries explicit enumeration/decidability data, Finite is a Prop-valued existence claim). Every Finite type admits a Fintype instance and vice versa, so the mathematical content is equivalent, but it is not literally the same typeclass as the gold.

Argument `f` is explicit in the produced statement (`(f : α → α)`) versus implicit in the gold (`{f : α → α}`), a minor binder-style difference that does not change the proposition but alters the call signature.
